infiniflow__ragflow@7051234.pr_summary: The PR adds CommonService.delete_by_ids and DocumentService.get_doc_ids_by_doc_names. UserCanvasVersionService.delete_all_versions now collects every version past the newest 20 and deletes them with one delete_by_ids call. The old code called `cls.delete(...)`, which does not exist on CommonService, so it raised AttributeError, the `except Exception` swallowed it and nothing was ever pruned. The external DELETE /v1/api/document handler (document_rm) now resolves doc_names with one `name IN (...)` query and pre-fetches the documents with get_by_ids instead of calling get_by_id once per document. So every request that sends doc_ids without matching doc_names (the ids-only shape) now fails and deletes nothing. The old list comprehension always gave a list.

langflow-ai__langflow@9513d15.pr_summary: The PR turns Vertex._log_transaction_async into a coroutine. Under `async with self._lock`, it gathers and clears the vertex's outstanding log_transaction tasks, then creates the new task. An outer `except asyncio.CancelledError` handler cancels whatever is left in the set, and wraps each `Task.cancel()` in `suppress(asyncio.CancelledError)`. The four call sites (Vertex._get_result at base.py:677/683 and ComponentVertex._get_result at vertex_types.py:110/149) now await it. The stated goal is to stop Loop flows raising SQLite "database is locked" when transaction-log tasks pile up.

defects.title: Non-reentrant vertex lock re-acquired inside get_result: every result lookup with a flow_id deadlocks
defects.statement: Vertex.get_result holds self._lock (a plain asyncio.Lock, which is not reentrant) while it awaits self._get_result. Both _get_result implementations now await _log_transaction_async, which does `async with self._lock` on the same lock, so the coroutine waits forever on a lock its own caller holds. Every graph with flow_id set (normal API/UI runs) hangs the first time a vertex resolves a predecessor's result, on both the success path and the not-built/error path. No transaction is ever logged and the flow never finishes.
defects.evidence: base.py:62 `self._lock = asyncio.Lock()`. base.py:621-622 `async with self._lock:\n    return await self._get_result(requester, target_handle_name)`. base.py:637 (inside the new async _log_transaction_async) `async with self._lock:`. base.py:683 `await self._log_transaction_async(str(flow_id), source=self, target=requester, status="success")` (and :677 for the error path), plus vertex_types.py:149/110 in the ComponentVertex override. Path: Graph.process creates build_vertex tasks -> Vertex.build (base.py:821) -> _build -> _build_each_vertex_in_params_dict -> _build_vertex_and_update_params / _build_list_of_vertices_and_update_params / _build_dict_and_update_params (base.py:688/702/601) -> `await predecessor.get_result(self, ...)` -> takes predecessor._lock -> predecessor._get_result -> `if flow_id: await self._log_transaction_async(...)` -> `async with self._lock` on the already-held lock, which never resolves. The only entry to _get_result is get_result (grep confirms), so every logged lookup is affected. At the merge base _log_transaction_async was synchronous and took no lock.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that _log_transaction_async acquires self._lock while its caller get_result already holds the same lock, and that asyncio.Lock is not reentrant, so the call deadlocks or hangs whenever flow_id is set. Pointing at either the lock acquisition (base.py:637) or any of the four awaited call sites is fine if the re-entrancy is named. Near-misses that do NOT count: generic 'awaiting logging adds latency / blocks on DB I/O' (R15, dataset ref 3); 'serializing under the lock hurts performance' with no deadlock; test requests that only mention 'a hang' as a hypothetical (R1, R12, R18, R22) without identifying the lock re-entry.

defects.title: suppress(asyncio.CancelledError) around Task.cancel() is ineffective dead code
defects.statement: The new outer cancellation handler wraps `pending_task.cancel()` in `with suppress(asyncio.CancelledError)`. Task.cancel() only schedules cancellation and never raises CancelledError in the caller, so the wrapper and the new `from contextlib import suppress` import do nothing. They mislead readers about which cancellation path is handled.
defects.evidence: base.py:658-659 `with suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):\n    pending_task.cancel()`; base.py:10 `from contextlib import suppress` was added only for this. asyncio.Task.cancel() returns a bool and delivers CancelledError inside the target task on its next step, never synchronously to the caller.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the suppress(CancelledError) around task.cancel() cannot catch anything, because cancel() does not raise in the caller, and so the wrapper is redundant or dead. Near-misses that do NOT count: a claim that the outer handler iterates an already-cleared set and therefore misses cancellations (dataset ref 1, which is wrong because the inner handler cancels the local list); generic 'simplify the task bookkeeping' (R16).

excluded.reason: Wrong. The inner `except asyncio.CancelledError` (base.py:644-649) already cancels the local `tasks` snapshot before re-raising, so the outer handler finding self.log_transaction_tasks empty drops no cancellation. Also, asyncio.gather cancels its children when it is cancelled. The outer loop is at most redundant.

Wrong on the exception claim: create_task does not raise, and log_transaction (graph/utils.py:141-167) catches every Exception, so gather over those tasks can only raise CancelledError and cannot mask the not-built ValueError. immich-app__immich@7e2009f.pr_summary: When an asset has no usable EXIF date tag, MetadataService.getDates now falls back to the earlier of asset.fileModifiedAt and asset.fileCreatedAt. Before, it always used fileCreatedAt. The aim is that a file copied before upload (new creation time, original modification time) keeps its original date. The warn message is reworded and a unicorn/prefer-math-min-max disable is added (the rule exists in the pinned eslint-plugin-unicorn 56.0.1). The PR also makes the Android/Samsung motion-photo path build the hidden motion-video asset's fileCreatedAt, fileModifiedAt and localDateTime from getDates(asset, tags) instead of copying the still's stored fileCreatedAt/fileModifiedAt. Two unit tests are added for the still-image fallback. Separately, the stale @tsconfig/docusaurus entry is removed from docs/package-lock.json; docs/package.json had already dropped it in #14755, so this only brings the lockfile back in sync. The existing motion-photo tests still pass because the stubs have equal created and modified dates and no date tags. The only verified defect is low severity: the motion-video path gives fileModifiedAt a different meaning.

defects.title: Motion-video asset's fileModifiedAt now comes from the still's EXIF ModifyDate, and that value then feeds the new min() fallback
defects.statement: When the PR creates the hidden motion-video asset, it now sets fileModifiedAt to getDates(asset, tags).modifyDate. That is the still image's EXIF ModifyDate whenever one is present. Before, it was the still's stored file modification timestamp, and every other writer stores a file or client mtime in that field. The video's own queued METADATA_EXTRACTION then goes through the PR's new fallback when the video has no date tags. The fallback treats fileModifiedAt as a file mtime and takes min(fileModifiedAt, fileCreatedAt). So the linked video's capture date can be replaced by the still's EXIF ModifyDate, or by an earlier stored mtime, and end up differing from, or earlier than, the photo's capture date. The API also exposes the EXIF value as the video's fileModifiedAt.
defects.evidence: Head metadata.service.ts:453-460 has `const dates = this.getDates(asset, tags); ... fileCreatedAt: dates.dateTimeOriginal, fileModifiedAt: dates.modifyDate, localDateTime: dates.localDateTime`. At the merge base it was `const createdAt = asset.fileCreatedAt ?? asset.createdAt; ... fileModifiedAt: asset.fileModifiedAt`. getDates lines 608-610: `let modifyDate = asset.fileModifiedAt; try { modifyDate = (exifTags.ModifyDate as ExifDateTime)?.toDate() ?? modifyDate; }`. Line 497 queues `JobName.METADATA_EXTRACTION` for the new motion asset. When that video has no EXIF_DATE_TAGS, line 601 takes `const earliestDate = asset.fileModifiedAt < asset.fileCreatedAt ? asset.fileModifiedAt : asset.fileCreatedAt;`, and line 222 writes the result into fileCreatedAt. Every other writer of fileModifiedAt stores an mtime: library.service.ts:410-411 and 514-515 (stat mtime), asset-media.service.ts:342 (client value), cli asset.ts:281 (stats.mtime). asset-response.dto.ts:134 exposes the field. Reach: a new Android/Samsung motion photo whose still carries an EXIF ModifyDate (or whose stored mtime is earlier than its EXIF capture instant), and whose embedded video has no usable date tag. The video is hidden, so the user-visible impact is small.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the motion-video creation now stores the still's EXIF ModifyDate (getDates().modifyDate) as the video's fileModifiedAt instead of the file modification timestamp, i.e. that the field's meaning or provenance changes. Also count a comment that explains how the dates written here, fed into the new earliest-of fallback in the video's own metadata extraction, can move the video's date off, or before, the photo's capture date. defects.title: A hole that welds down to zero points crashes the constructor inside earcut (TypeError)
defects.statement: cleanPoints compares with the last kept point and, at the wrap-around, compares points[0] with it. Once a ring is down to one point, that point is compared with itself (distance 0) and spliced, so a tiny or all-identical hole becomes []. With bevel enabled (the default), triangulateShape still registers a zero-length hole index, and earcut's eliminateHoles gets `undefined` from linkedList and dereferences `list.next`. `new ExtrudeGeometry` then throws on input that built fine at the merge base.
defects.evidence: L172-181: `const currentIndex = i % points.length; ... if ( distSq <= THRESHOLD_SQ ) { points.splice( currentIndex, 1 ); if ( currentIndex == 0 ) break;`. With length 1, currentIndex is 0 and currentPos === prevPos, so the last point is removed. L194 `holes.forEach( cleanPoints );`. src/extras/ShapeUtils.js triangulateShape still does `holeIndices.push( holeIndex )` for the empty hole. In earcut 3.0.1 (package.json), linkedList returns `undefined` when start===end, and eliminateHoles does `if (list === list.next)`, which throws. Measured by running the sources: a unit square with an absarc hole of radius 0.00005 builds at base (lid 168) but at head throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'next')`. A hole of three identical points builds at base (lid 24) and throws the same way at head. With bevel off there is no throw, only because triangulation is skipped (D1).
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that cleanPoints can reduce a hole (or ring) to zero points, and that the empty hole then breaks triangulation (throw/crash in triangulateShape or earcut). These do not count: saying only that small holes or contours are erased or lose detail (that is D3); dataset ref 1's claim that cleanPoints itself throws on empty or 1-point input via points[0].x (false: the loop is not entered, or it compares the point with itself); its `points.length < 2` guard, which would not prevent a longer ring collapsing to empty.

defects.title: Absolute 0.0002 world-unit weld threshold decimates or deletes valid small-scale shapes and holes
defects.statement: The threshold is a hard-coded world-space distance that ignores the shape's scale, and each point is measured against the last kept point. Any ring sampled more finely than 0.0002 loses vertices, and any contour or hole whose edges are all shorter than 0.0002 is spliced away entirely. Legitimate small-unit geometry that the merge base extruded faithfully now changes shape or produces no geometry at all, with no warning.
defects.evidence: L167-168 `const THRESHOLD = 0.0002; const THRESHOLD_SQ = THRESHOLD * THRESHOLD;`. L178-183 splice on `distSq <= THRESHOLD_SQ`. L187 `prevPos = currentPos;` runs only for kept points. L193 `cleanPoints( vertices );`. Measured by running the sources, base -> head: a 0.0001 square with bevel off went from lid 12 / side 24 to 0 / 0 (no geometry); with a small bevel it went from 12 / 168 to 0 / 0. A circle of radius 0.001 with curveSegments 48 went from lid 570 to 132, which is heavy decimation. Upstream later renamed this function to mergeOverlappingPoints and cut the threshold to about 1e-10, which is consistent with this being a real regression.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the fixed or absolute 0.0002 threshold (not scale-aware) removes vertices from legitimately small or densely sampled shapes, or erases small contours or holes entirely. These do not count: pure renaming or `===` style comments; R9's seam re-check edge case (a different, contrived issue); requests only for tests of near-threshold contours.

excluded.reason: Naming preference (rename cleanPoints to mergePoints). This is naming taste, not a defect with a concrete consequence.

The suggested `length < 2` guard also would not stop a longer ring collapsing to empty. The real related failure, an empty hole crashing earcut, is D2 and is a different mechanism.

Request to add a comment. Documentation nit.

Contrived and not a regression. Leaving a near-duplicate pair after the first point is spliced at the seam needs the closing point to lie between P0 and P1, which means the contour folds back on itself at the seam. The result is no worse than the merge base, which did no welding at all.
Style: `===` vs `==` on numeric comparisons, which behave identically.
The numHoles vs holes.length inconsistency is a style nit. The hole count cannot change, so both expressions are always equal. The main part of R4 is credited to D3.
Requests to add regression tests. Test requests are not defects, though the regressions they gesture at are D1 and D3.

A question about whether triangulating the bevel-offset (t==0) layer is intentional. It is the PR's stated purpose (the screenshots with negative bevelOffset), and the layer-0 and final top layer share that 2D shape, so the topology is correct when bevel is enabled. It does not identify the empty-array failure in D1.
Not raised as a defect. The O(n^2) splice inside the loop only matters for huge, heavily welded rings, which is not a realistic performance regression.

ollama__ollama@b6002f6.pr_summary: The PR changes input.Batch.Positions and input.Batch.Outputs from []int32 slices to ml.Tensor. The Ollama runner now builds both tensors once with ctx.Input().FromIntSlice (in reserveWorstCaseGraph, Outputs uses Arange), so the models stop building their own. llama4, mistral3 and qwen25vl TextModel.Forward now take the whole batch. The PR adds Tensor.Ints() to the ml.Tensor interface. In the ggml backend, Bytes(), Floats() and Ints() gain a fallback for tensors that were never computed: if ggml_get_data() is non-nil, they read that pointer as host memory (GoBytes copies it; Floats and Ints return unsafe.Slice views). The KV caches (Causal, Encoder, Wrapper) and llama4's attention-temperature loop read positions back from the tensor through Positions.Ints().

defects.title: Fit-mode graph reservation reads positions through a no-alloc placeholder pointer, so llama4 and mllama cannot load
defects.statement: The runner always runs LoadOperationFit first, with AllocMemory=false. In that mode FromIntSlice never writes the positions, and ggml gives the tensor a placeholder data pointer equal to the buffer alignment (about 0x20). The new Ints() branch returns unsafe.Slice over that non-nil pointer. reserveWorstCaseGraph then dereferences it in two places: in EncoderCache.StartForward (mllama; the reservation batch carries the dummy image) and in llama4's attention-temperature loop (on by default). The read faults and becomes a nil-dereference panic, allocModel turns it into an error, /load returns 500, and ollamaServer.Load fails. Both architectures require the Ollama engine, so they cannot be loaded at all. Before the PR both sites read a host []int32 slice.
defects.evidence: llm/server.go:709 `for operation := LoadOperationFit; operation < LoadOperationCommit; operation++` means Fit always runs first. runner.go:1204 `AllocMemory: req.Operation != llm.LoadOperationFit`, and ggml.go:162 `C.ggml_backend_buft_set_alloc(bt, C.bool(params.AllocMemory))` covers the CPU buffer type, which backs Input(). ggml-backend.cpp:47-51: when buft->no_alloc, a buffer is created with no memory. ggml-backend.cpp:135-137 `if (buffer->no_alloc) { return (void *)ggml_backend_buffer_get_alignment(buffer); }`, and ggml.go:882 `C.ggml_backend_tensor_alloc(b, t, C.ggml_backend_buffer_get_base(b))` sets tensor->data to that placeholder. ggml.go:931 `if c.b.allocMemory && len(s) > 0 { ggml_backend_tensor_set ... }` skips the copy. ggml.go:1035-1037 `} else if bts := C.ggml_get_data(t.t); bts != nil { data = unsafe.Slice((*int32)(bts), C.ggml_nelements(t.t)) }`. runner.go:1069 `batch.Positions = ctx.Input().FromIntSlice(batchPositions, ...)` is followed by :1074 `cache.StartForward(ctx, batch, true)` and :1080 `s.model.Forward(ctx, batch)`. encoder.go:94 `c.curPos = batch.Positions.Ints()[batch.Multimodal[len(batch.Multimodal)-1].Index]` runs even when reserve is true. mllama EncodeMultimodal only builds a graph and PostTokenize keeps inputs[0].Multimodal, so the reservation batch has a Multimodal entry, and mllama's WrapperCache calls the encoder cache first. llama4 model_text.go:204 `attentionTemperatureTuning: c.Bool("attention.temperature_tuning", true)` and :222 `for i, p := range batch.Positions.Ints()`. allocModel's recover turns the runtime error into panicErr, and load() then returns http 500. fs/ggml/ggml.go:241 OllamaEngineRequired lists "llama4" and "mllama". Causal's reserve path is not affected: it only takes len() and never dereferences the values.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that during the fit / no-alloc (AllocMemory=false) reservation, the positions tensor is never populated (or has only a placeholder data pointer), and that reading it back through Ints() in the encoder cache (mllama, encoder.go:94) or in llama4's temperature-scale loop (model_text.go:222) crashes or fails the model load. Naming one of the two read sites together with the fit-mode mechanism is enough. A comment on the Ints() branch or on runner.go:1069 also counts if it ties the placeholder read to the fit load crash. R2 and R19 count only weakly: they get the fit-mode root cause and (R2) the encoder-cache failure, but they wrongly say Ints() returns nil. Near-misses that do NOT count: generic advice to guard Ints() against a nil or short slice at encoder.go:94 (dataset ref 1; the slice has the correct length, the memory is invalid, and a length guard fixes nothing); claims that Causal gets curBatchSize=0 or under-reserves memory (R1, false: len() of the placeholder slice is correct); the host-vs-device-pointer contract (that is D2); and round-trip performance remarks.

defects.title: The new Bytes/Floats/Ints fallback treats any non-nil data pointer as readable, already-computed host memory
defects.statement: For tensors whose sync is nil, the added branch reads ggml_get_data() directly and assumes it is host memory that already holds the values. That fails in two cases. A tensor in a GPU buffer (for example a weight from Layer()) has a device pointer, and GoBytes or unsafe.Slice on it crashes the process. A pending op whose result is a view of an allocated destination (ggml_cpy returns a view of dst) has a non-nil pointer to memory that was never written. ml.Dump uses `t.Bytes() == nil` to decide whether to compute first, so it now skips computation and prints uninitialized data for F16/Q8_0/Q4_0 tensors (the Copy into an Input F32 buffer), or crashes on GPU-resident F32/I32 tensors. Before the PR it always computed first.
defects.evidence: ggml.go:1007-1009 `} else if bts := C.ggml_get_data(t.t); bts != nil { // tensor is in cpu memory; data = C.GoBytes(bts, C.int(C.ggml_nbytes(t.t)))`, with the same pattern at :1021-1024 (Floats) and :1035-1038 (Ints). ggml_get_data returns tensor->data whatever buffer holds it. ggml.c:3252 ggml_cpy_impl `struct ggml_tensor * result = ggml_view_tensor(ctx, b);` and ggml.c:1645 `void * data = view_src != NULL ? view_src->data : NULL;` give the cpy result the destination's host pointer before compute. backend.go:551-553 `f32 := ctx.Input().Empty(DTypeF32, ...); f32 = t.Copy(ctx, f32)`, then :567 `if t.Bytes() == nil { ctx.Forward(t).Compute(t) }` and :572 `binary.Read(bytes.NewBuffer(t.Bytes()), ...)`. At the merge base, Bytes() returned data only when t.sync != nil. ml.Dump has no in-tree callers; it is a developer debugging helper, which is why this is graded low.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that a non-nil ggml data pointer does not mean the data is host-accessible and/or already computed, with a consequence: a crash when reading a GPU/device-buffer tensor, or stale or uninitialized values for a pending or uncomputed tensor (for example ml.Dump skipping Compute because Bytes() is no longer nil). A suggestion to check ggml_backend_buffer_is_host or to keep the computed/uncomputed distinction also counts if it gives the reason. Near-misses that do NOT count: the fit-mode placeholder crash on its own (that is D1); the C.int truncation of GoBytes for tensors over 2 GiB (dataset ref 4); remarks that the function silently returns nil (dataset refs 5 and 6, same as pre-PR behaviour).

defects.title: Floats()/Ints() return a view into C memory on the new path but a Go-owned copy on the computed path, and Causal keeps the view after its context is freed
defects.statement: On the new branch, Floats() and Ints() return unsafe.Slice views into the tensor's ggml buffer. On the computed (sync) path they return freshly allocated Go copies, and Bytes() copies on both paths. Callers cannot tell whether the result outlives ctx.Close() or whether writing to it changes the tensor. Causal stores the view in the long-lived field c.curPositions, which dangles once the batch context is closed (computeBatch defers activeBatch.ctx.Close()). Today it is read only inside StartForward, so this is a latent use-after-free and aliasing hazard, not a live one.
defects.evidence: ggml.go:1024 `data = unsafe.Slice((*float32)(bts), C.ggml_nelements(t.t))` and :1038 `data = unsafe.Slice((*int32)(bts), C.ggml_nelements(t.t))` versus :1031-1034 `data = make([]int32, ...); ... ggml_backend_tensor_get(...)`. Context.Close (ggml.go) calls ggml_backend_buffer_free on every allocated buffer. causal.go:203 `c.curPositions = batch.Positions.Ints()` is a struct field declared at causal.go:66-67. runner.go computeBatch has `defer activeBatch.ctx.Close()`. The only current readers of curPositions (causal.go:221, 293-300, 364-366) run inside StartForward.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the new Floats/Ints path returns a slice aliasing C/ggml memory that is freed when the context closes (or that writes alias the tensor), inconsistent with the copying sync path, ideally noting that Causal retains it in curPositions. Near-misses that do NOT count: pure performance remarks about slice/tensor conversion (dataset refs 0 and 2); the host-vs-device pointer issue (D2); the fit-mode placeholder read (D1).

excluded.reason: The performance concern about the slice->tensor->slice round trip is not a real regression. On the host path Ints() is a zero-copy unsafe.Slice view, so there is no extra copy. The note is speculative and does not raise the fit-mode crash.

A generic nil/short-slice guard request. For a non-empty Positions tensor, Ints() never returns nil or a shorter slice; it returns the full length (real data, or the no-alloc placeholder). The real failure at this line is D1 (dereferencing unpopulated placeholder memory during fit), which this note does not identify and which its proposed length check would not fix.
Trivial hoisting/performance nit on the error-unwind path. Ints() is a zero-copy view, and Sequences and Positions are built together with equal length (model.Forward checks it).
Adding Ints() to the internal ml.Tensor interface does not break the build: both implementations (ggml Tensor and the kvcache testTensor) are updated in the PR, and grep finds no other implementers.

C.int truncation in the new Bytes() branch is reachable only for an uncomputed tensor over 2 GiB through Bytes(), whose only in-tree caller is the debug helper ml.Dump. It is speculative with no realistic path.
Returning nil when there is neither sync nor data is the pre-PR behaviour of Bytes(). It is not a regression, and the caller (ml.Dump) treats nil as 'compute first'.
Same as ref 5 for Ints(): a nil return for an unallocated zero-size tensor is consistent with Floats/Bytes, and no caller reaches it with a non-empty expectation. Speculative.
Typo in a comment that was only moved; a nit.

A nil Positions tensor in model.Forward is unreachable: its only callers (forwardBatch runner.go:582 and reserveWorstCaseGraph runner.go:1069) always set Positions, and forwardBatch returns early when the batch is empty.
Same as ref 8: a zero-value Batch with nil Positions is never passed to model.Forward by any in-tree caller. This is hardening, not a reachable defect.
batch.Outputs holds exactly the values the former explicit outputs argument was built from, so llama4's last-layer behaviour is unchanged.
Praise plus a generic 'ensure it doesn't fail silently' remark; no defect is identified.

Division by zero on an empty Outputs is pre-existing (len() was also 0 before) and unreachable: sampling only happens for sequences whose output row is in this batch, so Outputs is non-empty whenever this line runs.

False premise. In fit mode Ints() returns a non-nil, full-length slice over the placeholder pointer, so Causal's curBatchSize = len(curPositions) is correct and the reserved mask/graph size is not underestimated. Causal never dereferences the values when reserve is true.

Not a defect. In gptoss, Rows(outputs) is applied after the attention block, so the KV cache is still updated for every token of an intermediate chunk, and those chunks need no logits. Passing an empty outputs tensor to Rows is what llama, qwen2, qwen3 and gemma already did before this PR (they built FromIntSlice(batch.Outputs, 0) unconditionally), and ggml skips empty nodes. dbeaver__dbeaver@bc3ac7b.pr_summary: The PR fixes pasting Team Edition (remote) project files into a file-system (DBNPathBase) folder. DBNResource.getAdapter now returns a newly opened IFile.getContents() stream when asked for InputStream.class, and throws RuntimeException if that fails. DBNPathBase.dropNodes gets a new branch for nodes that have no Path adapter: it asks the node for that InputStream and writes it to folder/<node display name> through a new copyInputStream helper that calls Files.copy. The paste handler (NavigatorHandlerObjectCreateCopy) calls pathTarget.dropNodes directly without checking supportsDrop, so the branch is reached. The PR body says directories are still not handled.

defects.title: InputStream obtained for a pasted remote file is never closed
defects.statement: dropNodes gets a newly opened stream from node.getAdapter(InputStream.class), which calls IFile.getContents(), and passes it to copyInputStream. That helper calls Files.copy(InputStream, Path, ...), which does not close its source. Nothing else closes the stream either: there is no try-with-resources. Every pasted remote file therefore leaks one open content stream (a file handle or a remote connection), and the stream also leaks when resolve or Files.copy throws.
defects.evidence: DBNPathBase.java:293-296 at head reads `InputStream adapter = node.getAdapter(InputStream.class); if (adapter != null) { String fileName = node.getNodeDisplayName(); copyInputStream(adapter, folder, fileName); }`, and its `finally` only calls `monitor.worked(1)`. DBNPathBase.java:363-369 `copyInputStream(...) { ... Files.copy(inputStream, targetFile, options); }` has no close. DBNResource.java:425 `return adapter.cast(file.getContents());` opens a new stream on every call. The existing copy in NavigatorHandlerObjectCreateCopy.java:233 uses `try (InputStream is = ((IFile) resource).getContents())`. Reached from NavigatorHandlerObjectCreateCopy.java:100-103 (`pathTarget.dropNodes(monitor, cbNodes)`) when a TE resource with a null location is pasted into a file-system folder.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the InputStream from getAdapter(InputStream.class) / IFile.getContents() in the new dropNodes branch or in copyInputStream is never closed, for example because Files.copy does not close it or because there is no try-with-resources. Mentioning the failure path is optional. Near-misses that do not count: comments only about the redundant REPLACE_EXISTING check, the parameter name, or reusing DBNStreamData that never mention the stream staying open.

defects.title: New InputStream adapter duplicates the existing DBNStreamData.openInputStream contract
defects.statement: DBNResource already implements DBNStreamData. Its supportsStreamData() is true exactly for remote IFiles with no location, and openInputStream() opens the same IFile.getContents() stream and reports failure through checked IOException. The PR adds a second way to get that stream: getAdapter(InputStream.class). It has a side effect (every adapter lookup opens a caller-owned stream) and a different failure contract (it wraps CoreException in an unchecked RuntimeException). DBNPathBase lives in the same model bundle as DBNStreamData and could have used that interface. Two stream-opening paths for the same resource will drift apart, and a generic adapter probe now leaks or throws.
defects.evidence: New code at DBNResource.java:423-429 is `else if (adapter == InputStream.class && resource instanceof IFile file) { try { return adapter.cast(file.getContents()); } catch (CoreException e) { log.error(...); throw new RuntimeException(e); } }`. The existing code in the same class at :441-443 is `supportsStreamData() { return resource instanceof IFile && resource.getLocation() == null; }` and at :452-458 is `openInputStream() ... return file.getContents(); ... catch (CoreException e) { throw new IOException(e); }`. DBNStreamData is at plugins/org.jkiss.dbeaver.model/src/org/jkiss/dbeaver/model/navigator/DBNStreamData.java, in the same bundle as DBNPathBase. The existing consumer, NavigatorDragSourceListener.java:142, uses `nextSelected instanceof DBNStreamData streamData && streamData.supportsStreamData()`.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must point out that the new InputStream adapter duplicates DBNResource's existing DBNStreamData.openInputStream() / supportsStreamData() and that the paste path should use that contract, or must say that getAdapter opening a stream or throwing an unchecked exception is a bad adapter contract. A comment that only says 'close the stream' is D1, not this one. Generic remarks such as 'wrap in try/catch' or 'log the exception' do not count.

defects.title: DBNResource uses DBNNode's package-private `log` across OSGi bundles, so the error path throws IllegalAccessError
defects.statement: DBNResource declares no `log` field of its own, so the new `log.error(...)` binds to DBNNode's package-private `static final Log log`. DBNNode is in the org.jkiss.dbeaver.model bundle, while DBNResource is in the separate org.jkiss.dbeaver.model.rcp bundle, which reuses the same package name. The two classes are defined by different bundle class loaders, so they are in different runtime packages. The code compiles, but when file.getContents() throws CoreException the catch block fails with IllegalAccessError. The intended log line and RuntimeException(cause) never happen, and the paste fails with an 'Internal error' naming IllegalAccessError instead of the real content-read failure.
defects.evidence: DBNResource.java:427 `log.error("Error get file content");` is the only `log` reference in the file, and there is no Log field declaration. DBNNode.java:40 `static final Log log = Log.getLog(DBNNode.class);` is package-private. The org.jkiss.dbeaver.model.rcp MANIFEST.MF declares a standalone bundle (`Bundle-SymbolicName: org.jkiss.dbeaver.model.rcp`, `Require-Bundle: ... org.jkiss.dbeaver.model;visibility:=reexport`, `Export-Package: ... org.jkiss.dbeaver.model.navigator`), so the package is split across two bundles. Every other class in that rcp package declares its own `private static final Log log` (DBFResourceListener:32, DBNProjectDesktop:39, NavigatorResourceListener:31, NavigatorResources:44). UIUtils.runWithMonitor at UIUtils.java:1902-1906 turns the non-DBException target into `new DBException("Internal error", e.getTargetException())`.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that `log` in DBNResource is not declared there and resolves to DBNNode's package-private field across bundles / split package, and that this causes IllegalAccessError at runtime, or at least that it is an invalid cross-bundle access. A comment that only says the log message should include the exception or the file name is a nit and does not count. A comment claiming a compile error is wrong, because it compiles.

defects.title: Target file name comes from the node's display name instead of the resource's file name
defects.statement: The new branch names the copied file after node.getNodeDisplayName(), which is a UI label, not the file name. The existing Path branch uses resource.getFileName(). For DBNResource subclasses that override the display name, the copy gets the wrong name: DBNBookmark returns the bookmark title, so a pasted remote bookmark file loses its .bm extension and is named after its title. The label is also not sanitised before folder.resolve, so a separator in the title redirects or breaks the copy.
defects.evidence: DBNPathBase.java:295 `String fileName = node.getNodeDisplayName();` and :364 `Path targetFile = folder.resolve(str);`, while the existing branch at :320 uses `folder.resolve(resource.getFileName().toString())`. DBNBookmark.java:62-64 (extends DBNResource) is `public String getNodeDisplayName() { return storage.getTitle(); }`. The existing stream-to-file code at NavigatorDragSourceListener.java:168 escapes the name: `getTempFolder().resolve(CommonUtils.escapeFileName(fileName))`.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that using getNodeDisplayName() as the target file name is wrong: it is a display label rather than the resource or file name (for example, a bookmark title without its extension), or it is unsanitised and can contain path separators. Comments that only rename the `str` parameter do not count.

linera-io__linera-protocol@3535ddb.pr_summary: The validator's chain worker now caps the received_log slice in a ChainInfo response at CHAIN_INFO_MAX_RECEIVED_LOG_ENTRIES (1000) (state.rs:1416-1421). The client's synchronize_received_certificates_from_validator (client/mod.rs:846-857) now pages through the log, advancing the offset until a page returns fewer than 1000 entries. The server side is correct: LogView::read clamps end to count and returns an empty Vec when start >= end (log_view.rs:316-329). The client loop's only exit is a short page. Nothing bounds it by iterations, by progress, or by the count_received_log the response already carries, so a validator that keeps returning full pages keeps it running and growing memory. A validator hotfix also silently changes the contract for existing SDK clients: they make one request and now receive only the first 1000 unseen entries. Separately, the paging loop has the client assume the server's page size.

defects.title: Client pagination loop is unbounded: a validator returning full pages keeps it running forever and growing remote_log
defects.statement: The new loop in synchronize_received_certificates_from_validator exits only when a page has fewer than CHAIN_INFO_MAX_RECEIVED_LOG_ENTRIES entries. Nothing bounds iterations, checks for progress, or compares against count_received_log. The client verifies only the response signature, not that the entries belong to the requested offset. A faulty or Byzantine validator (or, in theory, log growth that outpaces paging) can therefore keep returning 1000-entry pages, and the client loops forever, appending to remote_log and never reaching certificate processing. On the per-validator notification path (process_notification -> find_received_certificates_from_validator) no timeout applies, so that task hangs while the client's memory grows without limit. Before this PR the client made a single request, bounded by the gRPC message limit.
defects.evidence: client/mod.rs:848-857 `loop { let query = ChainInfoQuery::new(chain_id).with_received_log_excluding_first_n(offset); let info = remote_node.handle_chain_info_query(query).await?; let received_entries = info.requested_received_log.len(); offset += received_entries as u64; remote_log.extend(info.requested_received_log); if received_entries < CHAIN_INFO_MAX_RECEIVED_LOG_ENTRIES { break; } }` has no other exit. remote_node.rs:150-162 check_and_return_info checks only the chain id of proposals and locking, plus `response.check(self.public_key)` (the signature), and never checks the log against the offset. Reach: process_notification (3696) on `Reason::NewIncomingBundle` calls `self.find_received_certificates_from_validator(remote_node).await?` (3712), which calls `synchronize_received_certificates_from_validator` directly (4026-4028), inside the per-validator listener task (3988-4003), with no timeout. Only find_received_certificates (2280-2294) goes through communicate_with_quorum, whose grace period eventually drops a slow validator. Merge base: a single `handle_chain_info_query` and `let remote_log = info.requested_received_log;` (merge-base client/mod.rs:845-847).
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say the new pagination loop can fail to terminate, or grows without bound, because its only exit is receiving a page shorter than the limit, and must name a trigger: a malicious or faulty validator that keeps returning full pages or ignores the offset, or entries being appended as fast as the client pages. It should ask for a bound: an iteration or size cap, a progress or offset check, or stopping at count_received_log taken from the first response. Comments that only call this a missing test ("add a test that the loop terminates") do not count. Neither does the observation that an exact multiple of 1000 costs one extra request, or the suggestion to break on `<=`.

defects.title: Hotfixed validators silently truncate the received log for existing (pre-PR) SDK clients
defects.statement: The PR ships as a validator hotfix. After it, every existing SDK client, which makes exactly one request_received_log_excluding_first_n query per sync and treats the vector it gets back as the complete tail, receives only the first 1000 unseen entries. Nothing in the response marks it as truncated, and legacy clients ignore count_received_log. For a chain with more than 1000 unseen entries, one sync by an old client now delivers only part of its incoming messages. Its tracker advances only past the returned entries, so it catches up only 1000 entries per later sync (or notification). Previously a single call returned the whole tail, for backlogs up to the gRPC size limit.
defects.evidence: state.rs:1418-1420 `let end = (start.saturating_add(CHAIN_INFO_MAX_RECEIVED_LOG_ENTRIES)).min(chain.received_log.count()); info.requested_received_log = chain.received_log.read(start..end).await?;` changes what the unchanged wire field returns: the doc on data_types.rs:215-217 still reads as "the response to request_received_certificates_excluding_first_n", and the request type carries no version or page flag. Legacy client (merge-base client/mod.rs:845-847): `let query = ChainInfoQuery::new(chain_id).with_received_log_excluding_first_n(tracker); let info = remote_node.handle_chain_info_query(query).await?; let remote_log = info.requested_received_log;`, with a single request and no paging. The tracker loop (merge base :925 onward, head :932-942) advances only over entries in remote_log. Release plan in the PR body: "be released in a new SDK, be released in a validator hotfix".
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the validator-side cap changes behaviour for older or already-deployed clients that make a single request: they silently get only the first 1000 entries per sync, so syncs are partial and catch-up is slow. Ideally it also suggests gating the cap behind a pagination-aware or versioned request, or at least acknowledges the rollout skew. Comments about the new client's loop, or about the server clamping arithmetic, do not count here. This is a deliberate trade-off: old clients still make progress and lose no data, so it is low severity.

lvgl__lvgl@4a57db3.pr_summary: The PR caches the label's measured text size in a new private field, lv_label_t.text_size, which lv_label_refr_text writes. In lv_label.c, draw_main's SCROLL and SCROLL_CIRCULAR paths now read that cache instead of calling lv_text_get_size. The PR also adds a public field, lv_draw_label_dsc_t.text_size, which lv_label copies into its draw descriptor. lv_draw_label_iterate_characters then uses that field as the line width when LV_TEXT_FLAG_EXPAND is set. In the steady state the output is unchanged. Under EXPAND, lv_text_get_size already forces max_width to LV_COORD_MAX, and lv_text_get_next_line ignores max_width, so both the cached size and the iterator's w match the old values or are unused. What remains: a public descriptor field that is dead and misleading, because only lv_label sets it and the value is ignored. Label drawing now depends on a cache that goes stale on the few paths that change the effective font without STYLE_CHANGED or SIZE_CHANGED. The duplicated Nema GFX iterator was not updated.

defects.title: New public lv_draw_label_dsc_t.text_size is dead and misleading: only lv_label sets it and its only consumer's value is ignored
defects.statement: The PR adds a public field to lv_draw_label_dsc_t, documented as 'The size of the text', and makes lv_draw_label_iterate_characters use dsc->text_size.x as the line width when EXPAND is set. Only lv_label's draw_main fills it. The roller, the table, the one-line textarea placeholder and any user code that sets LV_TEXT_FLAG_EXPAND pass the zeroed default {0,0}. This works only because the sole consumer passes w to lv_text_get_next_line, which returns early and ignores max_width whenever EXPAND is set. So the new public API field and its per-task copy carry nothing. Any future consumer, or any change that makes max_width matter under EXPAND, would get width 0 for every non-label producer.
defects.evidence: Head lv_draw_label.h:38-39 adds '/**The size of the text*/ lv_point_t text_size;' to the public descriptor. lv_draw_label.c:221 reads 'w = dsc->text_size.x;' in the EXPAND branch. w is used only as max_width in lv_text_get_next_line calls at lv_draw_label.c:259, 265 and 509. lv_text.c:336 is 'if((flag & LV_TEXT_FLAG_EXPAND) || (flag & LV_TEXT_FLAG_FIT)) { ... return i; }', so max_width is ignored. The only writer is lv_label.c:826 'label_draw_dsc.text_size = label->text_size;'. lv_draw_label_dsc_init (lv_draw_label.c:77) calls lv_memzero, so other EXPAND producers pass 0: roller.c:583 'label_dsc.flag |= LV_TEXT_FLAG_EXPAND;', table.c:837 'label_dsc_act.flag |= LV_TEXT_FLAG_EXPAND;' and textarea.c:1405 'if(ta->one_line) ph_dsc.flag |= LV_TEXT_FLAG_EXPAND;'. None of them sets text_size.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the new descriptor field (or the w it feeds) is unnecessary, dead or misleading. Either it says the value is ignored because lv_text_get_next_line disregards max_width under EXPAND, or it says only lv_label populates it, so other EXPAND users (roller, table, textarea placeholder, user code) pass 0. Asking to remove the field or to not read it in the iterator also counts. Near-misses that do NOT count: saying the draw-side value may be 'stale' or 'wrong after text updates' (at this site the value has no effect); 'uninitialized' claims; generic ABI or struct-size remarks with no mention of the field being unused or only set by the label.

defects.title: draw_main now uses a size cached at refr_text time; paths that change the effective font without STYLE_CHANGED/SIZE_CHANGED leave the alignment override and the circular second copy using a stale width
defects.statement: Before the PR, draw_main measured the text at draw time with the font and letter and line spacing actually used for drawing. It now reads label->text_size, which only lv_label_refr_text writes. refr_text runs only on LV_EVENT_STYLE_CHANGED or LV_EVENT_SIZE_CHANGED, or from the label setters. Some paths change the inherited or state font without either event: lv_obj_set_parent onto a parent with a different text_font, and a state change whose differing style also holds a draw-pad property (shadow, outline, transform), where update_obj_state only invalidates. On those paths the SCROLL_CIRCULAR second copy is placed at offset.x + the old width, so the copies overlap or leave a gap. The CENTER/RIGHT to LEFT override is also decided from the old width. The label's animation and self-size were already stale on these paths, so the regression is narrow.
defects.evidence: Head lv_label.c:894 'lv_point_t size = label->text_size;' then 898 'label_draw_dsc.ofs_x = label->offset.x + size.x + lv_font_get_glyph_width(label_draw_dsc.font, ...)', which mixes the cached width with the draw-time font. lv_label.c:856 does the same for the align override. The only writer is lv_label.c:968 'label->text_size = size;' in lv_label_refr_text. The event handler calls refr_text only for 'LV_EVENT_STYLE_CHANGED || LV_EVENT_SIZE_CHANGED' (lv_label.c:762). lv_obj.c:979-982: on LV_STYLE_STATE_CMP_DIFF_DRAW_PAD, update_obj_state only calls lv_obj_invalidate and lv_obj_refresh_ext_draw_size, with no refresh_style and therefore no STYLE_CHANGED to the object or its children. lv_obj_style_state_compare returns DRAW_PAD when a differing style has a shadow, outline or transform property, even if it also sets text_font. lv_obj_set_parent (lv_obj_tree.c:147-206) sends no style refresh. At the merge base, draw_main called lv_text_get_size(&size, label->text, label_draw_dsc.font, ...) at draw time.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must say that the SCROLL or SCROLL_CIRCULAR draw logic (alignment override or circular copy offset) now relies on label->text_size, which is refreshed only in lv_label_refr_text. It must also say that the value can go stale when the font, letter_space or line_space in effect at draw time changes without refr_text running, and that this gives a wrong copy offset or alignment. Near-misses that do NOT count: claims that a TEXT change can leave it stale (every text setter calls refr_text); claims about the stale value at lv_draw_label.c:221 (ignored there, see D1); 'uninitialized field' claims; the max_w vs LV_COORD_MAX claim (identical under EXPAND); size_cache vs text_size 'inconsistency' claims.

The Nema GFX backend keeps its own duplicated _draw_label_iterate_characters, and that copy was not updated. It still measures the whole text on every EXPAND label draw, so the claimed draw-time saving does not reach that backend, and the two copies of the routine now diverge.
defects.evidence: Head lv_draw_nema_gfx_label.c:140 calls '_draw_label_iterate_characters(t, dsc, coords);' and lines 438-441 keep 'lv_point_t p; lv_text_get_size(&p, dsc->text, dsc->font, dsc->letter_space, dsc->line_space, LV_COORD_MAX, dsc->flag); w = p.x;' in the EXPAND branch. The shared iterator at lv_draw_label.c:221 now reads 'w = dsc->text_size.x;'. The PR title is 'perf(label): reduce the time of calling lv_text_get_size when drawing'.
defects.notes: To count, a comment must point out that the Nema GFX label path (lv_draw_nema_gfx_label.c, its private iterator) still calls lv_text_get_size per draw and did not get the optimization or the matching change. A question form ('should Nema also...') counts. Near-misses that do NOT count: generic 'other backends may need updating' with no mention of Nema GFX or a duplicated iterator.
